obligation: Covered telecommunications or video surveillance equipment identified (Section 889)
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d)(1)-(2); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: The company identifies, or is told by a supplier or any other source, that covered telecommunications or video surveillance equipment or services are used as a substantial or essential component of any system during contract performance (for example a covered or rebranded product on a DoD order)
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification or notification; further information on mitigation and prevention within 10 business days of the first report. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: DoD: https://dibnet.dod.mil (identify the contract and order numbers); tell the Federal Prime the same day for its orders
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - FAR 52.204-25 is in all 34 DoD orders

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c)(1)-(2); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: The company identifies, or is notified of, a Kaspersky Lab covered article provided to the Government during contract performance, under an order that includes FAR 52.204-23
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification or notification; further information within 10 business days of the first report. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: DoD: https://dibnet.dod.mil; otherwise the contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: Only for orders that include FAR 52.204-23; check each purchase order (the company resells security software licenses)

obligation: Electronic parts from outside the sourcing order, or not confirmed new
trigger: A product for a DoD order came from a source other than the original manufacturer, its authorized suppliers, or an approved supplier, or cannot be confirmed as new and unused (for example a broker item, or a unit with signs of tampering or reuse)
deadline: Promptly, in writing; keep inspection, testing, and authentication records for the Government on request
notify: Contracting officer (direct DoD orders); the Federal Prime for its orders
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - DoD setup orders and Federal Prime orders

trigger: Becoming aware or having reason to suspect that an item bought for delivery to the Government is counterfeit or suspect counterfeit
deadline: Within 60 days: written notice to the contracting officer and a GIDEP report; keep the items until disposition instructions
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an order includes the clause. None of the 34 DoD orders does (FAR 46.317 prescribes it mainly for DoD electronic parts acquisitions above the simplified acquisition threshold); check each new order

obligation: DFARS cyber incident report affecting covered defense information
trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident affecting a covered contractor information system or the covered defense information in it
notify: DoD (DIBNet portal; requires a DoD-approved medium assurance certificate); subcontractors also notify the prime
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no covered defense information, so it has no covered contractor information system (P03 G-027). Recheck if CUI is ever received

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (for example employee records, or customer portal user names with passwords, exposed through a compromised mailbox or vendor)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (a 15-day extension is possible for good cause shown in writing to the Department within 30 days)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if company-held personal information is involved

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (no extension for this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - the company holds personal information on 7 employees and about 60 customer portal users; check the count in each incident

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
applies_at_this_tier: No at the company's current data volumes; check each incident

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a third-party agent of the company (the MSP, the ERP vendor, the payroll service)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents of other states (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it
applies_at_this_tier: Check the residence of each affected person; apply the law of each state where they live

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand is made. All U.S. persons

obligation: Business email compromise and payment fraud report
trigger: A supplier or company mailbox is used to request a bank change or payment, whether or not money moved
deadline: Voluntary; file as soon as possible, and call the bank fraud desk at once to try to recall any payment
applies_at_this_tier: Yes (voluntary). The April 2026 diversion was not reported; report future cases

obligation: Notice to customers who received suspect products
trigger: Suspect counterfeit, tampered, or covered items were shipped to a commercial customer or the Federal Prime
deadline: As each contract requires; otherwise promptly once serials are confirmed
notify: Affected customers in writing (serials, what is known, hold or return instructions)

trigger: Suspected security incident, payment fraud, or supplier compromise involving company systems
deadline: Per policy: call the 24x7 breach hotline before engaging any incident vendor; use panel counsel and forensics ($10,000 retention)

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Public company determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is privately held

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident / ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity (as defined in the final rule)
deadline: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment) - not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final
